title: Schauder Projection Lemma
description: The Schauder projection lemma: given a compact set K in a normed space and epsilon > 0, there exists a continuous map approximating the identity on K with image in a finite-dimensional convex hull. Proved from first principles using partition of unity.

overview.historicalContext:
The Schauder projection lemma is a key technical tool in functional analysis, introduced by Juliusz Schauder in 1930. It provides the crucial finite-dimensional approximation step in the proof of the Schauder fixed point theorem, which generalizes Brouwer's theorem to infinite-dimensional spaces.

The lemma says that any compact set in a normed space can be 'almost projected' onto a finite-dimensional convex hull. This bridge between infinite and finite dimensions is what allows the Brouwer theorem (which only works in finite dimensions) to be leveraged in the infinite-dimensional setting.
overview.problemStatement:
Given a compact set $K$ in a normed space $E$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, prove there exist finitely many points $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in K$ and a continuous map $\pi: E \to E$ such that:
1. $\pi(K) \subseteq \mathrm{conv}\{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$
2. $\|\pi(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ for all $x \in K$
overview.text: The Schauder projection lemma: given a compact set K in a normed space and epsilon > 0, there exists a continuous map approximating the identity on K with image in a finite-dimensional convex hull. Proved from first principles using partition of unity.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof constructs the projection explicitly using a partition of unity:

1. **Finite cover**: By compactness, cover $K$ by finitely many $\varepsilon$-balls $B(x_i, \varepsilon)$ centered at points of $K$.

2. **Bump functions**: Define $\varphi_i(x) = \max(0, \varepsilon - \|x - x_i\|)$. Each $\varphi_i$ is continuous, nonneg, and positive exactly on $B(x_i, \varepsilon)$.

3. **Projection map**: Define $\pi(x) = \sum_i \varphi_i(x) \cdot x_i / \sum_i \varphi_i(x)$. The denominator is positive on $K$ since the balls cover $K$.

4. **Properties**: $\pi$ is continuous (quotient of continuous functions with positive denominator), maps into the convex hull (it's a convex combination), and $\|\pi(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ (only nearby centers contribute to the weighted average).
keyInsights: The partition of unity trick: bump functions phi_i(x) = max(0, eps - ||x - x_i||) provide a smooth way to weight contributions from nearby centers
The weighted average is automatically a convex combination (nonneg weights summing to 1)
The approximation bound follows because only centers within distance epsilon contribute (others have zero weight)
This lemma is the key step reducing infinite-dimensional fixed point problems to finite-dimensional ones
The proof is fully constructive: the projection map is explicitly defined (not merely shown to exist), making it amenable to computation and algorithmic extraction

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring, Mathlib imports for topology, convex analysis, and normed spaces. Opens namespaces and declares variables for normed space $E$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
sections.mathContext: Setting: $(E, \|\cdot\|)$ a real normed space, $K \subseteq E$ compact, $\varepsilon > 0$. Goal: construct continuous $\pi: E \to \text{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ with $\|\pi(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ on $K$.

sections.title: Convex Hull Compactness
sections.summary: Two auxiliary results: the convex hull of a finite set is closed, and the convex hull of a finite range is compact.
sections.mathContext: $S$ finite $\Rightarrow \text{conv}(S)$ is closed (in finite dimensions) and compact.

sections.title: Bump Function Infrastructure
sections.summary: Defines bump functions $\varphi_i(x) = \max(0, \varepsilon - \|x - c_i\|)$ and proves: nonnegativity, continuity, positivity in $B(c_i, \varepsilon)$, and vanishing outside $B(c_i, \varepsilon)$.

sections.title: Sum of Bumps and Positivity
sections.summary: The sum $\Phi(x) = \sum_i \varphi_i(x)$ is continuous and positive on $K$ (since the $\varepsilon$-balls cover $K$).

sections.title: The Schauder Projection Map
sections.summary: Defines the Schauder projection $\pi(x) = \sum_i \varphi_i(x) \cdot c_i / \Phi(x)$ as a weighted average of centers.
sections.mathContext: $\pi(x) = \frac{\sum_i \varphi_i(x) c_i}{\sum_i \varphi_i(x)}$, a convex combination of the centers $c_1, \ldots, c_n$.

sections.title: Properties of the Projection
sections.summary: Three key properties proved: (1) continuity on $K$ (quotient of continuous functions with positive denominator), (2) image in convex hull (convex combination), (3) $\varepsilon$-approximation ($\|\pi(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ since only nearby centers contribute).

sections.title: Main Theorem
sections.summary: The Schauder projection lemma: combines compactness (finite subcover), bump function construction, and the three properties into the complete result.
sections.mathContext: For compact $K \subseteq E$ and $\varepsilon > 0$: $\exists$ finitely many $c_i \in K$ and continuous $\pi: E \to \text{conv}\{c_i\}$ with $\|\pi(x) - x\| < \varepsilon$ on $K$.

sections.title: Applications: Convex Hull Results
sections.summary: Corollaries: compactness and closedness of convex hulls of finite ranges, resolving a sorry in SchauderFixedPoint.lean.

crossReferences.description: The projection lemma is the key technical ingredient: it approximates a compact operator by finite-rank operators, reducing the infinite-dimensional Schauder theorem to the finite-dimensional Brouwer theorem. This entry resolves a sorry in SchauderFixedPoint.lean

Schauder's theorem generalizes Brouwer's from finite to infinite dimensions: the projection lemma maps into a finite-dimensional convex hull where Brouwer applies, then the approximation argument lifts the fixed point back to the infinite-dimensional space

Both are topological fixed-point theorems with roots in algebraic topology. Borsuk-Ulam proves that any continuous map $S^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ has a pair of antipodal points with the same image — a deeper result that implies Brouwer's theorem. The projection lemma here provides the functional-analytic bridge from finite-dimensional topology (Brouwer/Borsuk-Ulam) to infinite-dimensional fixed-point theory (Schauder)

conclusion.summary: The Schauder projection lemma has been proved completely from first principles, with zero sorries and zero axioms. The proof constructs an explicit partition of unity using bump functions and verifies all required properties: continuity, convex hull membership, and epsilon-approximation.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This result is the key technical ingredient for proving the Schauder fixed point theorem.

Combined with the Brouwer fixed point theorem in finite dimensions, it yields: every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a normed space has a fixed point. The proof also provides convex hull compactness results that resolve a sorry in the existing SchauderFixedPoint.lean formalization.
openQuestions: Can the projection be made globally continuous (not just on K) via Tietze extension?
What is the optimal number of centers needed for a given epsilon?
Can the bump functions be replaced with smoother (C-infinity) partition of unity functions?
